text: For hatred does not cease by hatred at any time: hatred ceases by love, this is an old rule.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 5 · bản Anh F. Max Müller
vi: Hận thù không thể chấm dứt bằng hận thù; chỉ tình thương mới làm hận thù lắng xuống.

text: The world does not know that we must all come to an end here;--but those who know it, their quarrels cease at once.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 6 · bản Anh F. Max Müller
vi: Khi hiểu rằng đời người rồi sẽ kết thúc, ta có thể buông những tranh chấp.

text: They who know truth in truth, and untruth in untruth, arrive at truth, and follow true desires.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 12 · bản Anh F. Max Müller
vi: Nhận ra điều chân thật là chân thật, điều sai là sai, ta mới có thể đến với sự thật.

text: As rain does not break through a well-thatched house, passion will not break through a well-reflecting mind.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 14 · bản Anh F. Max Müller
vi: Như mái nhà được lợp kín không để mưa lọt qua, tâm được rèn luyện không dễ bị dục vọng xâm nhập.

text: The thoughtless man, even if he can recite a large portion (of the law), but is not a doer of it, has no share in the priesthood, but is like a cowherd counting the cows of others.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 19 · bản Anh F. Max Müller
vi: Đọc nhiều lời dạy mà không thực hành giống như người chăn bò chỉ đếm đàn bò của người khác.

text: If an earnest person has roused himself, if he is not forgetful, if his deeds are pure, if he acts with consideration, if he restrains himself, and lives according to law,--then his glory will increase.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 24 · bản Anh F. Max Müller
vi: Sống tỉnh thức, hành động trong sạch, suy xét cẩn thận và biết tự chủ, phẩm hạnh sẽ lớn lên.

text: By rousing himself, by earnestness, by restraint and control, the wise man may make for himself an island which no flood can overwhelm.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 25 · bản Anh F. Max Müller
vi: Bằng sự chuyên cần và tự chủ, người trí tạo cho mình một hòn đảo mà nước lũ không thể nhấn chìm.

text: Fools follow after vanity, men of evil wisdom. The wise man keeps earnestness as his best jewel.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 26 · bản Anh F. Max Müller
vi: Người trí gìn giữ sự tỉnh thức như báu vật quý nhất.

text: Follow not after vanity, nor after the enjoyment of love and lust! He who is earnest and meditative, obtains ample joy.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 27 · bản Anh F. Max Müller
vi: Người chuyên cần và biết thiền quán tìm được niềm vui sâu sắc.

text: As a fletcher makes straight his arrow, a wise man makes straight his trembling and unsteady thought, which is difficult to guard, difficult to hold back.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 33 · bản Anh F. Max Müller
vi: Như người thợ nắn thẳng mũi tên, người trí rèn luyện tâm vốn chao đảo và khó giữ.

text: It is good to tame the mind, which is difficult to hold in and flighty, rushing wherever it listeth; a tamed mind brings happiness.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 35 · bản Anh F. Max Müller
vi: Tâm khó giữ và thường chạy theo ý thích; điều phục được tâm đem lại hạnh phúc.

text: Let the wise man guard his thoughts, for they are difficult to perceive, very artful, and they rush wherever they list: thoughts well guarded bring happiness.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 36 · bản Anh F. Max Müller
vi: Hãy gìn giữ tâm ý tinh tế, khó nhận biết; tâm được bảo hộ đem lại hạnh phúc.

text: Not a mother, not a father will do so much, nor any other relative; a well-directed mind will do us greater service.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 43 · bản Anh F. Max Müller
vi: Một tâm được hướng đúng đem lại lợi ích lớn hơn cả sự giúp đỡ của người thân.

text: As the bee collects nectar and departs without injuring the flower, or its colour or scent, so let a sage dwell in his village.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 49 · bản Anh F. Max Müller
vi: Như ong lấy mật mà không làm hại sắc hương của hoa, người hiền sống giữa đời cũng vậy.

text: Not the perversities of others, not their sins of commission or omission, but his own misdeeds and negligences should a sage take notice of.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 50 · bản Anh F. Max Müller
vi: Đừng chỉ nhìn lỗi người khác; hãy xem xét những điều mình đã làm và đã bỏ quên.

text: Like a beautiful flower, full of colour, but without scent, are the fine but fruitless words of him who does not act accordingly.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 51 · bản Anh F. Max Müller
vi: Lời hay mà không đi đôi với hành động giống như hoa đẹp nhưng không hương.

text: But, like a beautiful flower, full of colour and full of scent, are the fine and fruitful words of him who acts accordingly.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 52 · bản Anh F. Max Müller
vi: Lời hay đi đôi với việc làm giống như đóa hoa vừa đẹp vừa thơm.

text: As many kinds of wreaths can be made from a heap of flowers, so many good things may be achieved by a mortal when once he is born.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 53 · bản Anh F. Max Müller
vi: Như nhiều vòng hoa được kết từ một đống hoa, một đời người có thể làm nhiều điều thiện.

text: All that we are is the result of what we have thought: it is founded on our thoughts, it is made up of our thoughts. If a man speaks or acts with an evil thought, pain follows him, as the wheel follows the foot of the ox that draws the carriage.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 1 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: His accurate examination of things in consultations, and patient hearing of others.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: All that we are is the result of what we have thought: it is founded on our thoughts, it is made up of our thoughts. If a man speaks or acts with a pure thought, happiness follows him, like a shadow that never leaves him.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 2 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: He would not hastily give over the search of the matter, as one easy to be satisfied with sudden notions and apprehensions.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: "He abused me, he beat me, he defeated me, he robbed me,"--in those who harbour such thoughts hatred will never cease.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 3 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: His care to preserve his friends; how neither at any time he would carry himself towards them with disdainful neglect, and grow weary of them; nor yet at any time be madly fond of them.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: "He abused me, he beat me, he defeated me, he robbed me,"--in those who do not harbour such thoughts hatred will cease.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 4 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: His contented mind in all things, his cheerful countenance, his care to foresee things afar off, and to take order for the least, without any noise or clamour.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Moreover how all acclamations and flattery were repressed by him: how carefully he observed all things necessary to the government, and kept an account of the common expenses, and how patiently he did abide that he was reprehended by some for this his strict and rigid kind of dealing.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: How he was neither a superstitious worshipper of the gods, nor an ambitious pleaser of men, or studious of popular applause; but sober in all things, and everywhere observant of that which was fitting; no affecter of novelties: in those things which conduced to his ease and convenience, (plenty whereof his fortune did afford him,) without pride and bragging, yet with all freedom and liberty: so that as he did freely enjoy them without any anxiety or affectation when they were present; so when absent, he found no want of them.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He who lives looking for pleasures only, his senses uncontrolled, immoderate in his food, idle, and weak, Mara (the tempter) will certainly overthrow him, as the wind throws down a weak tree.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 7 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Moreover, that he was never commended by any man, as either a learned acute man, or an obsequious officious man, or a fine orator; but as a ripe mature man, a perfect sound man; one that could not endure to be flattered; able to govern both himself and others.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He who lives without looking for pleasures, his senses well controlled, moderate in his food, faithful and strong, him Mara will certainly not overthrow, any more than the wind throws down a rocky mountain.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 8 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Again, how he was not easily moved and tossed up and down, but loved to be constant, both in the same places and businesses; and how after his great fits of headache he would return fresh and vigorous to his wonted affairs.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He who wishes to put on the yellow dress without having cleansed himself from sin, who disregards temperance and truth, is unworthy of the yellow dress.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 9 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Again, that secrets he neither had many, nor often, and such only as concerned public matters: his discretion and moderation, in exhibiting of the public sights and shows for the pleasure and pastime of the people: in public buildings. congiaries, and the like.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: But he who has cleansed himself from sin, is well grounded in all virtues, and regards also temperance and truth, he is indeed worthy of the yellow dress.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 10 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: In all these things, having a respect unto men only as men, and to the equity of the things themselves, and not unto the glory that might follow.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: They who imagine truth in untruth, and see untruth in truth, never arrive at truth, but follow vain desires.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 11 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Never wont to use the baths at unseasonable hours; no builder; never curious, or solicitous, either about his meat, or about the workmanship, or colour of his clothes, or about anything that belonged to external beauty.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: In all his conversation, far from all inhumanity, all boldness, and incivility, all greediness and impetuosity; never doing anything with such earnestness, and intention, that a man could say of him, that he did sweat about it: but contrariwise, all things distinctly, as at leisure; without trouble; orderly, soundly, and agreeably.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: As rain breaks through an ill-thatched house, passion will break through an unreflecting mind.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 13 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: A man might have applied that to him, which is recorded of Socrates, that he knew how to want, and to enjoy those things, in the want whereof, most men show themselves weak; and in the fruition, intemperate: but to hold out firm and constant, and to keep within the compass of true moderation and sobriety in either estate, is proper to a man, who hath a perfect and invincible soul; such as he showed himself in the sickness of Maximus.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: From the gods I received that I had good grandfathers, and parents, a good sister, good masters, good domestics, loving kinsmen, almost all that I have; and that I never through haste and rashness transgressed against any of them, notwithstanding that my disposition was such, as that such a thing (if occasion had been) might very well have been committed by me, but that It was the mercy of the gods, to prevent such a concurring of matters and occasions, as might make me to incur this blame.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The evil-doer mourns in this world, and he mourns in the next; he mourns in both. He mourns and suffers when he sees the evil of his own work.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 15 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: That I was not long brought up by the concubine of my father; that I preserved the flower of my youth.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The virtuous man delights in this world, and he delights in the next; he delights in both. He delights and rejoices, when he sees the purity of his own work.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 16 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: That I took not upon me to be a man before my time, but rather put it off longer than I needed.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The evil-doer suffers in this world, and he suffers in the next; he suffers in both. He suffers when he thinks of the evil he has done; he suffers more when going on the evil path.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 17 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: That I lived under the government of my lord and father, who would take away from me all pride and vainglory, and reduce me to that conceit and opinion that it was not impossible for a prince to live in the court without a troop of guards and followers, extraordinary apparel, such and such torches and statues, and other like particulars of state and magnificence; but that a man may reduce and contract himself almost to the state of a private man, and yet for all that not to become the more base and remiss in those public matters and affairs, wherein power and authority is requisite.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The virtuous man is happy in this world, and he is happy in the next; he is happy in both. He is happy when he thinks of the good he has done; he is still more happy when going on the good path.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 18 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: That I have had such a brother, who by his own example might stir me up to think of myself; and by his respect and love, delight and please me.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: That I have got ingenuous children, and that they were not born distorted, nor with any other natural deformity.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The follower of the law, even if he can recite only a small portion (of the law), but, having forsaken passion and hatred and foolishness, possesses true knowledge and serenity of mind, he, caring for nothing in this world or that to come, has indeed a share in the priesthood.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 20 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: That I was no great proficient in the study of rhetoric and poetry, and of other faculties, which perchance I might have dwelt upon, if I had found myself to go on in them with success.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Earnestness is the path of immortality (Nirvana), thoughtlessness the path of death. Those who are in earnest do not die, those who are thoughtless are as if dead already.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 21 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: That I did by times prefer those, by whom I was brought up, to such places and dignities, which they seemed unto me most to desire; and that I did not put them off with hope and expectation, that (since that they were yet but young) I would do the same hereafter.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Those who are advanced in earnestness, having understood this clearly, delight in earnestness, and rejoice in the knowledge of the Ariyas (the elect).
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 22 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: That I never had to do with Benedicta and Theodotus, yea and afterwards when I fell into some fits of love, I was soon cured.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: These wise people, meditative, steady, always possessed of strong powers, attain to Nirvana, the highest happiness.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 23 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: That having been often displeased with Rusticus, I never did him anything for which afterwards I had occasion to repent.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: That it being so that my mother was to die young, yet she lived with me all her latter years.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: That as often as I had a purpose to help and succour any that either were poor, or fallen into some present necessity, I never was answered by my officers that there was not ready money enough to do it; and that I myself never had occasion to require the like succour from any other.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: That I had choice of fit and able men, to whom I might commit the bringing up of my children.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: That by dreams I have received help, as for other things, so in particular, how I might stay my casting of blood, and cure my dizziness, as that also that happened to thee in Cajeta, as unto Chryses when he prayed by the seashore.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: When the learned man drives away vanity by earnestness, he, the wise, climbing the terraced heights of wisdom, looks down upon the fools, serene he looks upon the toiling crowd, as one that stands on a mountain looks down upon them that stand upon the plain.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 28 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: And when I did first apply myself to philosophy, that I did not fall into the hands of some sophists, or spent my time either in reading the manifold volumes of ordinary philosophers, nor in practising myself in the solution of arguments and fallacies, nor dwelt upon the studies of the meteors, and other natural curiosities.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Earnest among the thoughtless, awake among the sleepers, the wise man advances like a racer, leaving behind the hack.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 29 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: All these things without the assistance of the gods, and fortune, could not have been.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: By earnestness did Maghavan (Indra) rise to the lordship of the gods. People praise earnestness; thoughtlessness is always blamed.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 30 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Betimes in the morning say to thyself, This day I shalt have to do with an idle curious man, with an unthankful man, a railer, a crafty, false, or an envious man; an unsociable uncharitable man.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: A Bhikshu (mendicant) who delights in earnestness, who looks with fear on thoughtlessness, moves about like fire, burning all his fetters, small or large.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 31 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: All these ill qualities have happened unto them, through ignorance of that which is truly good and truly bad.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: A Bhikshu (mendicant) who delights in reflection, who looks with fear on thoughtlessness, cannot fall away (from his perfect state)--he is close upon Nirvana.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 32 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Whatsoever I am, is either flesh, or life, or that which we commonly call the mistress and overruling part of man; reason.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Away with thy books, suffer not thy mind any more to be distracted, and carried to and fro; for it will not be; but as even now ready to die, think little of thy flesh: blood, bones, and a skin; a pretty piece of knit and twisted work, consisting of nerves, veins and arteries; think no more of it, than so.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: As a fish taken from his watery home and thrown on dry ground, our thought trembles all over in order to escape the dominion of Mara (the tempter).
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 34 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: And as for thy life, consider what it is; a wind; not one constant wind neither, but every moment of an hour let out, and sucked in again.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The third, is thy ruling part; and here consider; Thou art an old man; suffer not that excellent part to be brought in subjection, and to become slavish: suffer it not to be drawn up and down with unreasonable and unsociable lusts and motions, as it were with wires and nerves; suffer it not any more, either to repine at anything now present, or to fear and fly anything to come, which the destiny hath appointed thee.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Whatsoever proceeds from the gods immediately, that any man will grant totally depends from their divine providence.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Those who bridle their mind which travels far, moves about alone, is without a body, and hides in the chamber (of the heart), will be free from the bonds of Mara (the tempter).
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 37 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: As for those things that are commonly said to happen by fortune, even those must be conceived to have dependence from nature, or from that first and general connection, and concatenation of all those things, which more apparently by the divine providence are administered and brought to pass.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If a man's thoughts are unsteady, if he does not know the true law, if his peace of mind is troubled, his knowledge will never be perfect.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 38 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: All things flow from thence: and whatsoever it is that is, is both necessary, and conducing to the whole (part of which thou art), and whatsoever it is that is requisite and necessary for the preservation of the general, must of necessity for every particular nature, be good and behoveful.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If a man's thoughts are not dissipated, if his mind is not perplexed, if he has ceased to think of good or evil, then there is no fear for him while he is watchful.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 39 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: And as for the whole, it is preserved, as by the perpetual mutation and conversion of the simple elements one into another, so also by the mutation, and alteration of things mixed and compounded.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Knowing that this body is (fragile) like a jar, and making this thought firm like a fortress, one should attack Mara (the tempter) with the weapon of knowledge, one should watch him when conquered, and should never rest.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 40 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Let these things suffice thee; let them be always unto thee, as thy general rules and precepts.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Before long, alas! this body will lie on the earth, despised, without understanding, like a useless log.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 41 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: As for thy thirst after books, away with it with all speed, that thou die not murmuring and complaining, but truly meek and well satisfied, and from thy heart thankful unto the gods.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Whatever a hater may do to a hater, or an enemy to an enemy, a wrongly-directed mind will do us greater mischief.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 42 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Remember how long thou hast already put off these things, and how often a certain day and hour as it were, having been set unto thee by the gods, thou hast neglected it.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: It is high time for thee to understand the true nature both of the world, whereof thou art a part; and of that Lord and Governor of the world, from whom, as a channel from the spring, thou thyself didst flow: and that there is but a certain limit of time appointed unto thee, which if thou shalt not make use of to calm and allay the many distempers of thy soul, it will pass away and thou with it, and never after return.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Who shall overcome this earth, and the world of Yama (the lord of the departed), and the world of the gods? Who shall find out the plainly shown path of virtue, as a clever man finds out the (right) flower?
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 44 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Let it be thy earnest and incessant care as a Roman and a man to perform whatsoever it is that thou art about, with true and unfeigned gravity, natural affection, freedom and justice: and as for all other cares, and imaginations, how thou mayest ease thy mind of them.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The disciple will overcome the earth, and the world of Yama, and the world of the gods. The disciple will find out the plainly shown path of virtue, as a clever man finds out the (right) flower.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 45 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Which thou shalt do; if thou shalt go about every action as thy last action, free from all vanity, all passionate and wilful aberration from reason, and from all hypocrisy, and self-love, and dislike of those things, which by the fates or appointment of God have happened unto thee.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He who knows that this body is like froth, and has learnt that it is as unsubstantial as a mirage, will break the flower-pointed arrow of Mara, and never see the king of death.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 46 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Thou seest that those things, which for a man to hold on in a prosperous course, and to live a divine life, are requisite and necessary, are not many, for the gods will require no more of any man, that shall but keep and observe these things.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Death carries off a man who is gathering flowers and whose mind is distracted, as a flood carries off a sleeping village.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 47 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Do, soul, do; abuse and contemn thyself; yet a while and the time for thee to respect thyself, will be at an end.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Death subdues a man who is gathering flowers, and whose mind is distracted, before he is satiated in his pleasures.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 48 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Every man's happiness depends from himself, but behold thy life is almost at an end, whiles affording thyself no respect, thou dost make thy happiness to consist in the souls, and conceits of other men.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Why should any of these things that happen externally, so much distract thee?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Give thyself leisure to learn some good thing, and cease roving and wandering to and fro.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Thou must also take heed of another kind of wandering, for they are idle in their actions, who toil and labour in this life, and have no certain scope to which to direct all their motions, and desires.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: For not observing the state of another man's soul, scarce was ever any man known to be unhappy.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Tell whosoever they be that intend not, and guide not by reason and discretion the motions of their own souls, they must of necessity be unhappy.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The scent of flowers does not travel against the wind, nor (that of) sandal-wood, or of Tagara and Mallika flowers; but the odour of good people travels even against the wind; a good man pervades every place.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 54 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: These things thou must always have in mind: What is the nature of the universe, and what is mine—in particular: This unto that what relation it hath: what kind of part, of what kind of universe it is: And that there is nobody that can hinder thee, but that thou mayest always both do and speak those things which are agreeable to that nature, whereof thou art a part.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Sandal-wood or Tagara, a lotus-flower, or a Vassiki, among these sorts of perfumes, the perfume of virtue is unsurpassed.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 55 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Theophrastus, where he compares sin with sin (as after a vulgar sense such things I grant may be compared:) says well and like a philosopher, that those sins are greater which are committed through lust, than those which are committed through anger.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Mean is the scent that comes from Tagara and sandal-wood;--the perfume of those who possess virtue rises up to the gods as the highest.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 56 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For he that is angry seems with a kind of grief and close contraction of himself, to turn away from reason; but he that sins through lust, being overcome by pleasure, doth in his very sin bewray a more impotent, and unmanlike disposition.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Of the people who possess these virtues, who live without thoughtlessness, and who are emancipated through true knowledge, Mara, the tempter, never finds the way.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 57 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Well then and like a philosopher doth he say, that he of the two is the more to be condemned, that sins with pleasure, than he that sins with grief.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Long is the night to him who is awake; long is a mile to him who is tired; long is life to the foolish who do not know the true law.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 60 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For indeed this latter may seem first to have been wronged, and so in some manner through grief thereof to have been forced to be angry, whereas he who through lust doth commit anything, did of himself merely resolve upon that action.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If a traveller does not meet with one who is his better, or his equal, let him firmly keep to his solitary journey; there is no companionship with a fool.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 61 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Whatsoever thou dost affect, whatsoever thou dost project, so do, and so project all, as one who, for aught thou knowest, may at this very present depart out of this life.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: "These sons belong to me, and this wealth belongs to me," with such thoughts a fool is tormented. He himself does not belong to himself; how much less sons and wealth?
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 62 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: And as for death, if there be any gods, it is no grievous thing to leave the society of men.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The fool who knows his foolishness, is wise at least so far. But a fool who thinks himself wise, he is called a fool indeed.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 63 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: But if it be so that there be no gods, or that they take no care of the world, why should I desire to live in a world void of gods, and of all divine providence?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If a fool be associated with a wise man even all his life, he will perceive the truth as little as a spoon perceives the taste of soup.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 64 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: But gods there be certainly, and they take care for the world; and as for those things which be truly evil, as vice and wickedness, such things they have put in a man's own power, that he might avoid them if he would: and had there been anything besides that had been truly bad and evil, they would have had a care of that also, that a man might have avoided it.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If an intelligent man be associated for one minute only with a wise man, he will soon perceive the truth, as the tongue perceives the taste of soup.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 65 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: But why should that be thought to hurt and prejudice a man's life in this world, which cannot any ways make man himself the better, or the worse in his own person?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Fools of little understanding have themselves for their greatest enemies, for they do evil deeds which must bear bitter fruits.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 66 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Neither must we think that the nature of the universe did either through ignorance pass these things, or if not as ignorant of them, yet as unable either to prevent, or better to order and dispose them.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: That deed is not well done of which a man must repent, and the reward of which he receives crying and with a tearful face.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 67 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: It cannot be that she through want either of power or skill, should have committed such a thing, so as to suffer all things both good and bad, equally and promiscuously, to happen unto all both good and bad.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: No, that deed is well done of which a man does not repent, and the reward of which he receives gladly and cheerfully.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 68 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: As for life therefore, and death, honour and dishonour, labour and pleasure, riches and poverty, all these things happen unto men indeed, both good and bad, equally; but as things which of themselves are neither good nor bad; because of themselves, neither shameful nor praiseworthy.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: As long as the evil deed done does not bear fruit, the fool thinks it is like honey; but when it ripens, then the fool suffers grief.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 69 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Consider how quickly all things are dissolved and resolved: the bodies and substances themselves, into the matter and substance of the world: and their memories into the general age and time of the world.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Let a fool month after month eat his food (like an ascetic) with the tip of a blade of Kusa grass, yet he is not worth the sixteenth particle of those who have well weighed the law.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 70 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Consider the nature of all worldly sensible things; of those especially, which either ensnare by pleasure, or for their irksomeness are dreadful, or for their outward lustre and show are in great esteem and request, how vile and contemptible, how base and corruptible, how destitute of all true life and being they are.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: An evil deed, like newly-drawn milk, does not turn (suddenly); smouldering, like fire covered by ashes, it follows the fool.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 71 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: It is the part of a man endowed with a good understanding faculty, to consider what they themselves are in very deed, from whose bare conceits and voices, honour and credit do proceed: as also what it is to die, and how if a man shall consider this by itself alone, to die, and separate from it in his mind all those things which with it usually represent themselves unto us, he can conceive of it no otherwise, than as of a work of nature, and he that fears any work of nature, is a very child.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: And when the evil deed, after it has become known, brings sorrow to the fool, then it destroys his bright lot, nay, it cleaves his head.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 72 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Now death, it is not only a work of nature, but also conducing to nature.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Let the fool wish for a false reputation, for precedence among the Bhikshus, for lordship in the convents, for worship among other people!
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 73 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Consider with thyself how man, and by what part of his, is joined unto God, and how that part of man is affected, when it is said to be diffused.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: "May both the layman and he who has left the world think that this is done by me; may they be subject to me in everything which is to be done or is not to be done," thus is the mind of the fool, and his desire and pride increase.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 74 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: There is nothing more wretched than that soul, which in a kind of circuit compasseth all things, searching (as he saith) even the very depths of the earth; and by all signs and conjectures prying into the very thoughts of other men's souls; and yet of this, is not sensible, that it is sufficient for a man to apply himself wholly, and to confine all his thoughts and cares to the tendance of that spirit which is within him, and truly and really to serve him.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: "One is the road that leads to wealth, another the road that leads to Nirvana;" if the Bhikshu, the disciple of Buddha, has learnt this, he will not yearn for honour, he will strive after separation from the world.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 75 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: His service doth consist in this, that a man keep himself pure from all violent passion and evil affection, from all rashness and vanity, and from all manner of discontent, either in regard of the gods or men.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If you see an intelligent man who tells you where true treasures are to be found, who shows what is to be avoided, and administers reproofs, follow that wise man; it will be better, not worse, for those who follow him.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 76 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For indeed whatsoever proceeds from the gods, deserves respect for their worth and excellency; and whatsoever proceeds from men, as they are our kinsmen, should by us be entertained, with love, always; sometimes, as proceeding from their ignorance, of that which is truly good and bad, (a blindness no less, than that by which we are not able to discern between white and black:) with a kind of pity and compassion also.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Let him admonish, let him teach, let him forbid what is improper!--he will be beloved of the good, by the bad he will be hated.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 77 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: If thou shouldst live three thousand, or as many as ten thousands of years, yet remember this, that man can part with no life properly, save with that little part of life, which he now lives: and that which he lives, is no other, than that which at every instant he parts with.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Do not have evil-doers for friends, do not have low people for friends: have virtuous people for friends, have for friends the best of men.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 78 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: That then which is longest of duration, and that which is shortest, come both to one effect.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He who drinks in the law lives happily with a serene mind: the sage rejoices always in the law, as preached by the elect (Ariyas).
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 79 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For although in regard of that which is already past there may be some inequality, yet that time which is now present and in being, is equal unto all men.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Well-makers lead the water (wherever they like); fletchers bend the arrow; carpenters bend a log of wood; wise people fashion themselves.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 80 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: And that being it which we part with whensoever we die, it doth manifestly appear, that it can be but a moment of time, that we then part with.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: As a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, wise people falter not amidst blame and praise.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 81 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For as for that which is either past or to come, a man cannot be said properly to part with it.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Wise people, after they have listened to the laws, become serene, like a deep, smooth, and still lake.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 82 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: First, that all things in the world from all eternity, by a perpetual revolution of the same times and things ever continued and renewed, are of one kind and nature; so that whether for a hundred or two hundred years only, or for an infinite space of time, a man see those things which are still the same, it can be no matter of great moment.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Good people walk on whatever befall, the good do not prattle, longing for pleasure; whether touched by happiness or sorrow wise people never appear elated or depressed.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 83 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: And secondly, that that life which any the longest liver, or the shortest liver parts with, is for length and duration the very same, for that only which is present, is that, which either of them can lose, as being that only which they have; for that which he hath not, no man can truly be said to lose.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If, whether for his own sake, or for the sake of others, a man wishes neither for a son, nor for wealth, nor for lordship, and if he does not wish for his own success by unfair means, then he is good, wise, and virtuous.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 84 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Remember that all is but opinion and conceit, for those things are plain and apparent, which were spoken unto Monimus the Cynic; and as plain and apparent is the use that may be made of those things, if that which is true and serious in them, be received as well as that which is sweet and pleasing.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Few are there among men who arrive at the other shore (become Arhats); the other people here run up and down the shore.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 85 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: A man's soul doth wrong and disrespect itself first and especially, when as much as in itself lies it becomes an aposteme, and as it were an excrescency of the world, for to be grieved and displeased with anything that happens in the world, is direct apostacy from the nature of the universe; part of which, all particular natures of the world, are.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: But those who, when the law has been well preached to them, follow the law, will pass across the dominion of death, however difficult to overcome.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 86 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Secondly, when she either is averse from any man, or led by contrary desires or affections, tending to his hurt and prejudice; such as are the souls of them that are angry.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Those whose mind is well grounded in the (seven) elements of knowledge, who without clinging to anything, rejoice in freedom from attachment, whose appetites have been conquered, and who are full of light, are free (even) in this world.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 89 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Fourthly, when she doth dissemble, and covertly and falsely either doth or saith anything.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: There is no suffering for him who has finished his journey, and abandoned grief, who has freed himself on all sides, and thrown off all fetters.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 90 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Fifthly, when she doth either affect or endeavour anything to no certain end, but rashly and without due ratiocination and consideration, how consequent or inconsequent it is to the common end.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: They depart with their thoughts well-collected, they are not happy in their abode; like swans who have left their lake, they leave their house and home.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 91 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For even the least things ought not to be done, without relation unto the end; and the end of the reasonable creatures is, to follow and obey him, who is the reason as it were, and the law of this great city, and ancient commonwealth.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Men who have no riches, who live on recognised food, who have perceived void and unconditioned freedom (Nirvana), their path is difficult to understand, like that of birds in the air.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 92 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: The time of a man's life is as a point; the substance of it ever flowing, the sense obscure; and the whole composition of the body tending to corruption.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He whose appetites are stilled, who is not absorbed in enjoyment, who has perceived void and unconditioned freedom (Nirvana), his path is difficult to understand, like that of birds in the air.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 93 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: His soul is restless, fortune uncertain, and fame doubtful; to be brief, as a stream so are all things belonging to the body; as a dream, or as a smoke, so are all that belong unto the soul.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The gods even envy him whose senses, like horses well broken in by the driver, have been subdued, who is free from pride, and free from appetites.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 94 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: And philosophy doth consist in this, for a man to preserve that spirit which is within him, from all manner of contumelies and injuries, and above all pains or pleasures; never to do anything either rashly, or feignedly, or hypocritically: wholly to depend from himself and his own proper actions: all things that happen unto him to embrace contentedly, as coming from Him from whom he himself also came; and above all things, with all meekness and a calm cheerfulness, to expect death, as being nothing else but the resolution of those elements, of which every creature is composed.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Such a one who does his duty is tolerant like the earth, like Indra's bolt; he is like a lake without mud; no new births are in store for him.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 95 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: And if the elements themselves suffer nothing by this their perpetual conversion of one into another, that dissolution, and alteration, which is so common unto all, why should it be feared by any?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: His thought is quiet, quiet are his word and deed, when he has obtained freedom by true knowledge, when he has thus become a quiet man.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 96 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: A man must not only consider how daily his life wasteth and decreaseth, but this also, that if he live long, he cannot be certain, whether his understanding shall continue so able and sufficient, for either discreet consideration, in matter of businesses; or for contemplation: it being the thing, whereon true knowledge of things both divine and human, doth depend.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The man who is free from credulity, but knows the uncreated, who has cut all ties, removed all temptations, renounced all desires, he is the greatest of men.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 97 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For if once he shall begin to dote, his respiration, nutrition, his imaginative, and appetitive, and other natural faculties, may still continue the same: he shall find no want of them.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: In a hamlet or in a forest, in the deep water or on the dry land, wherever venerable persons (Arhanta) dwell, that place is delightful.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 98 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: But how to make that right use of himself that he should, how to observe exactly in all things that which is right and just, how to redress and rectify all wrong, or sudden apprehensions and imaginations, and even of this particular, whether he should live any longer or no, to consider duly; for all such things, wherein the best strength and vigour of the mind is most requisite; his power and ability will be past and gone.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Forests are delightful; where the world finds no delight, there the passionless will find delight, for they look not for pleasures.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 99 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Thou must hasten therefore; not only because thou art every day nearer unto death than other, but also because that intellective faculty in thee, whereby thou art enabled to know the true nature of things, and to order all thy actions by that knowledge, doth daily waste and decay: or, may fail thee before thou die.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Even though a speech be a thousand (of words), but made up of senseless words, one word of sense is better, which if a man hears, he becomes quiet.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 100 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: This also thou must observe, that whatsoever it is that naturally doth happen to things natural, hath somewhat in itself that is pleasing and delightful: as a great loaf when it is baked, some parts of it cleave as it were, and part asunder, and make the crust of it rugged and unequal, and yet those parts of it, though in some sort it be against the art and intention of baking itself, that they are thus cleft and parted, which should have been and were first made all even and uniform, they become it well nevertheless, and have a certain peculiar property, to stir the appetite.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Even though a Gatha (poem) be a thousand (of words), but made up of senseless words, one word of a Gatha is better, which if a man hears, he becomes quiet.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 101 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: So figs are accounted fairest and ripest then, when they begin to shrink, and wither as it were.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Though a man recite a hundred Gathas made up of senseless words, one word of the law is better, which if a man hears, he becomes quiet.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 102 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: So ripe olives, when they are next to putrefaction, then are they in their proper beauty.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If one man conquer in battle a thousand times thousand men, and if another conquer himself, he is the greatest of conquerors.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 103 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: The hanging down of grapes—the brow of a lion, the froth of a foaming wild boar, and many other like things, though by themselves considered, they are far from any beauty, yet because they happen naturally, they both are comely, and delightful; so that if a man shall with a profound mind and apprehension, consider all things in the world, even among all those things which are but mere accessories and natural appendices as it were, there will scarce appear anything unto him, wherein he will not find matter of pleasure and delight.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If a man for a hundred years sacrifice month after month with a thousand, and if he but for one moment pay homage to a man whose soul is grounded (in true knowledge), better is that homage than sacrifice for a hundred years.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 106 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: So will he behold with as much pleasure the true rictus of wild beasts, as those which by skilful painters and other artificers are imitated.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If a man for a hundred years worship Agni (fire) in the forest, and if he but for one moment pay homage to a man whose soul is grounded (in true knowledge), better is that homage than sacrifice for a hundred years.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 107 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: So will he be able to perceive the proper ripeness and beauty of old age, whether in man or woman: and whatsoever else it is that is beautiful and alluring in whatsoever is, with chaste and continent eyes he will soon find out and discern.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Whatever a man sacrifice in this world as an offering or as an oblation for a whole year in order to gain merit, the whole of it is not worth a quarter (a farthing); reverence shown to the righteous is better.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 108 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Those and many other things will he discern, not credible unto every one, but unto them only who are truly and familiarly acquainted, both with nature itself, and all natural things.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He who always greets and constantly reveres the aged, four things will increase to him, viz. life, beauty, happiness, power.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 109 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: The Chaldeans and Astrologians having foretold the deaths of divers, were afterwards themselves surprised by the fates.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: But he who lives a hundred years, vicious and unrestrained, a life of one day is better if a man is virtuous and reflecting.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 110 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Alexander and Pompeius, and Caius Cæsar, having destroyed so many towns, and cut off in the field so many thousands both of horse and foot, yet they themselves at last were fain to part with their own lives.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: And he who lives a hundred years, ignorant and unrestrained, a life of one day is better if a man is wise and reflecting.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 111 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Heraclitus having written so many natural tracts concerning the last and general conflagration of the world, died afterwards all filled with water within, and all bedaubed with dirt and dung without.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: And he who lives a hundred years, idle and weak, a life of one day is better if a man has attained firm strength.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 112 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Lice killed Democritus; and Socrates, another sort of vermin, wicked ungodly men.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: And he who lives a hundred years, not seeing beginning and end, a life of one day is better if a man sees beginning and end.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 113 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Thou hast taken ship, thou hast sailed, thou art come to land, go out, if to another life, there also shalt thou find gods, who are everywhere.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: And he who lives a hundred years, not seeing the immortal place, a life of one day is better if a man sees the immortal place.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 114 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: If all life and sense shall cease, then shalt thou cease also to be subject to either pains or pleasures; and to serve and tend this vile cottage; so much the viler, by how much that which ministers unto it doth excel; the one being a rational substance, and a spirit, the other nothing but earth and blood.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: And he who lives a hundred years, not seeing the highest law, a life of one day is better if a man sees the highest law.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 115 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Spend not the remnant of thy days in thoughts and fancies concerning other men, when it is not in relation to some common good, when by it thou art hindered from some other better work.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If a man would hasten towards the good, he should keep his thought away from evil; if a man does what is good slothfully, his mind delights in evil.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 116 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: That is, spend not thy time in thinking, what such a man doth, and to what end: what he saith, and what he thinks, and what he is about, and such other things or curiosities, which make a man to rove and wander from the care and observation of that part of himself, which is rational, and overruling.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If a man commits a sin, let him not do it again; let him not delight in sin: pain is the outcome of evil.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 117 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: One who not often, nor without some great necessity tending to some public good, mindeth what any other, either speaks, or doth, or purposeth: for those things only that are in his own power, or that are truly his own, are the objects of his employments, and his thoughts are ever taken up with those things, which of the whole universe are by the fates or Providence destinated and appropriated unto himself.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If a man does what is good, let him do it again; let him delight in it: happiness is the outcome of good.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 118 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Those things that are his own, and in his own power, he himself takes order, for that they be good: and as for those that happen unto him, he believes them to be so.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Even an evil-doer sees happiness as long as his evil deed has not ripened; but when his evil deed has ripened, then does the evil-doer see evil.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 119 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For that lot and portion which is assigned to every one, as it is unavoidable and necessary, so is it always profitable.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Even a good man sees evil days, as long as his good deed has not ripened; but when his good deed has ripened, then does the good man see happy days.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 120 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: He remembers besides that whatsoever partakes of reason, is akin unto him, and that to care for all men generally, is agreeing to the nature of a man: but as for honour and praise, that they ought not generally to be admitted and accepted of from all, but from such only, who live according to nature.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Let no man think lightly of evil, saying in his heart, It will not come nigh unto me. Even by the falling of water-drops a water-pot is filled; the fool becomes full of evil, even if he gather it little by little.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 121 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: As for them that do not, what manner of men they be at home, or abroad; day or night, how conditioned themselves with what manner of conditions, or with men of what conditions they moil and pass away the time together, he knoweth, and remembers right well, he therefore regards not such praise and approbation, as proceeding from them, who cannot like and approve themselves.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Let no man think lightly of good, saying in his heart, It will not come nigh unto me. Even by the falling of water-drops a water-pot is filled; the wise man becomes full of good, even if he gather it little by little.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 122 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Do nothing against thy will, nor contrary to the community, nor without due examination, nor with reluctancy.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Let a man avoid evil deeds, as a merchant, if he has few companions and carries much wealth, avoids a dangerous road; as a man who loves life avoids poison.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 123 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Moreover, let thy God that is in thee to rule over thee, find by thee, that he hath to do with a man; an aged man; a sociable man; a Roman; a prince; one that hath ordered his life, as one that expecteth, as it were, nothing but the sound of the trumpet, sounding a retreat to depart out of this life with all expedition.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He who has no wound on his hand, may touch poison with his hand; poison does not affect one who has no wound; nor is there evil for one who does not commit evil.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 124 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: One who for his word or actions neither needs an oath, nor any man to be a witness.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If a man offend a harmless, pure, and innocent person, the evil falls back upon that fool, like light dust thrown up against the wind.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 125 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: To be cheerful, and to stand in no need, either of other men's help or attendance, or of that rest and tranquillity, which thou must be beholding to others for.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Some people are born again; evil-doers go to hell; righteous people go to heaven; those who are free from all worldly desires attain Nirvana.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 126 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Rather like one that is straight of himself, or hath ever been straight, than one that hath been rectified.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Not in the sky, not in the midst of the sea, not if we enter into the clefts of the mountains, is there known a spot in the whole world where a man might be freed from an evil deed.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 127 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: If thou shalt find anything in this mortal life better than righteousness, than truth, temperance, fortitude, and in general better than a mind contented both with those things which according to right and reason she doth, and in those, which without her will and knowledge happen unto thee by the providence; if I say, thou canst find out anything better than this, apply thyself unto it with thy whole heart, and that which is best wheresoever thou dost find it, enjoy freely.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Not in the sky, not in the midst of the sea, not if we enter into the clefts of the mountains, is there known a spot in the whole world where death could not overcome (the mortal).
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 128 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For it is not lawful, that anything that is of another and inferior kind and nature, be it what it will, as either popular applause, or honour, or riches, or pleasures; should be suffered to confront and contest as it were, with that which is rational, and operatively good.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: All men tremble at punishment, all men fear death; remember that you are like unto them, and do not kill, nor cause slaughter.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 129 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For all these things, if once though but for a while, they begin to please, they presently prevail, and pervert a man's mind, or turn a man from the right way.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: All men tremble at punishment, all men love life; remember that thou art like unto them, and do not kill, nor cause slaughter.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 130 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Thou art now ready to die, and yet hast thou not attained to that perfect simplicity: thou art yet subject to many troubles and perturbations; not yet free from all fear and suspicion of external accidents; nor yet either so meekly disposed towards all men, as thou shouldest; or so affected as one, whose only study and only wisdom is, to be just in all his actions.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He who seeking his own happiness punishes or kills beings who also long for happiness, will not find happiness after death.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 131 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Behold and observe, what is the state of their rational part; and those that the world doth account wise, see what things they fly and are afraid of; and what things they hunt after.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He who seeking his own happiness does not punish or kill beings who also long for happiness, will find happiness after death.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 132 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: In another man's mind and understanding thy evil Cannot subsist, nor in any proper temper or distemper of the natural constitution of thy body, which is but as it were the coat or cottage of thy soul.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Do not speak harshly to anybody; those who are spoken to will answer thee in the same way. Angry speech is painful, blows for blows will touch thee.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 133 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Wherein then, but in that part of thee, wherein the conceit, and apprehension of any misery can subsist?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If, like a shattered metal plate (gong), thou utter not, then thou hast reached Nirvana; contention is not known to thee.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 134 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Let not that part therefore admit any such conceit, and then all is well.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: As a cowherd with his staff drives his cows into the stable, so do Age and Death drive the life of men.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 135 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Though thy body which is so near it should either be cut or burnt, or suffer any corruption or putrefaction, yet let that part to which it belongs to judge of these, be still at rest; that is, let her judge this, that whatsoever it is, that equally may happen to a wicked man, and to a good man, is neither good nor evil.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: A fool does not know when he commits his evil deeds: but the wicked man burns by his own deeds, as if burnt by fire.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 136 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For that which happens equally to him that lives according to nature, and to him that doth not, is neither according to nature, nor against it; and by consequent, neither good nor bad.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Or lightning-fire will burn his houses; and when his body is destroyed, the fool will go to hell.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 140 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Ever consider and think upon the world as being but one living substance, and having but one soul, and how all things in the world, are terminated into one sensitive power; and are done by one general motion as it were, and deliberation of that one soul; and how all things that are, concur in the cause of one another's being, and by what manner of connection and concatenation all things happen.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Not nakedness, not platted hair, not dirt, not fasting, or lying on the earth, not rubbing with dust, not sitting motionless, can purify a mortal who has not overcome desires.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 141 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: What art thou, that better and divine part excepted, but as Epictetus said well, a wretched soul, appointed to carry a carcass up and down?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He who, though dressed in fine apparel, exercises tranquillity, is quiet, subdued, restrained, chaste, and has ceased to find fault with all other beings, he indeed is a Brahmana, an ascetic (sramana), a friar (bhikshu).
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 142 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: To suffer change can be no hurt; as no benefit it is, by change to attain to being.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Is there in this world any man so restrained by humility that he does not mind reproof, as a well-trained horse the whip?
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 143 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: The age and time of the world is as it were a flood and swift current, consisting of the things that are brought to pass in the world.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Like a well-trained horse when touched by the whip, be ye active and lively, and by faith, by virtue, by energy, by meditation, by discernment of the law you will overcome this great pain (of reproof), perfect in knowledge and in behaviour, and never forgetful.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 144 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For as soon as anything hath appeared, and is passed away, another succeeds, and that also will presently out of sight.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Well-makers lead the water (wherever they like); fletchers bend the arrow; carpenters bend a log of wood; good people fashion themselves.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 145 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Whatsoever doth happen in the world, is, in the course of nature, as usual and ordinary as a rose in the spring, and fruit in summer.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: How is there laughter, how is there joy, as this world is always burning? Why do you not seek a light, ye who are surrounded by darkness?
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 146 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Of the same nature is sickness and death; slander, and lying in wait, and whatsoever else ordinarily doth unto fools use to be occasion either of joy or sorrow.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Look at this dressed-up lump, covered with wounds, joined together, sickly, full of many thoughts, which has no strength, no hold!
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 147 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: That, whatsoever it is, that comes after, doth always very naturally, and as it were familiarly, follow upon that which was before.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: This body is wasted, full of sickness, and frail; this heap of corruption breaks to pieces, life indeed ends in death.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 148 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For thou must consider the things of the world, not as a loose independent number, consisting merely of necessary events; but as a discreet connection of things orderly and harmoniously disposed.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Those white bones, like gourds thrown away in the autumn, what pleasure is there in looking at them?
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 149 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: There is then to be seen in the things of the world, not a bare succession, but an admirable correspondence and affinity.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: After a stronghold has been made of the bones, it is covered with flesh and blood, and there dwell in it old age and death, pride and deceit.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 150 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Let that of Heraclitus never be out of thy mind, that the death of earth, is water, and the death of water, is air; and the death of air, is fire; and so on the contrary.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn
