text: The brilliant chariots of kings are destroyed, the body also approaches destruction, but the virtue of good people never approaches destruction,--thus do the good say to the good.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 151 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Even as if any of the gods should tell thee, Thou shalt certainly die to-morrow, or next day, thou wouldst not, except thou wert extremely base and pusillanimous, take it for a great benefit, rather to die the next day after, than to-morrow; (for alas, what is the difference!) so, for the same reason, think it no great matter to die rather many years after, than the very next day.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: A man who has learnt little, grows old like an ox; his flesh grows, but his knowledge does not grow. 153, 154. Looking for the maker of this tabernacle, I shall have to run through a course of many births, so long as I do not find (him); and painful is birth again and again. But now, maker of the tabernacle, thou hast been seen; thou shalt not make up this tabernacle again. All thy rafters are broken, thy ridge-pole is sundered; the mind, approaching the Eternal (visankhara, nirvana), has attained to the extinction of all desires.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 152 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Let it be thy perpetual meditation, how many physicians who once looked so grim, and so theatrically shrunk their brows upon their patients, are dead and gone themselves.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Men who have not observed proper discipline, and have not gained treasure in their youth, perish like old herons in a lake without fish.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 155 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: How many astrologers, after that in great ostentation they had foretold the death of some others, how many philosophers after so many elaborate tracts and volumes concerning either mortality or immortality; how many brave captains and commanders, after the death and slaughter of so many; how many kings and tyrants, after they had with such horror and insolency abused their power upon men's lives, as though themselves had been immortal; how many, that I may so speak, whole cities both men and towns: Helice, Pompeii, Herculaneum, and others innumerable are dead and gone.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Men who have not observed proper discipline, and have not gained treasure in their youth, lie, like broken bows, sighing after the past.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 156 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Run them over also, whom thou thyself, one after another, hast known in thy time to drop away.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If a man hold himself dear, let him watch himself carefully; during one at least out of the three watches a wise man should be watchful.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 157 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Such and such a one took care of such and such a one's burial, and soon after was buried himself.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Let each man direct himself first to what is proper, then let him teach others; thus a wise man will not suffer.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 158 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For herein lieth all indeed, ever to look upon all worldly things, as things for their continuance, that are but for a day: and for their worth, most vile, and contemptible, as for example, What is man?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If a man make himself as he teaches others to be, then, being himself well subdued, he may subdue (others); one's own self is indeed difficult to subdue.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 159 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: That which but the other day when he was conceived was vile snivel; and within few days shall be either an embalmed carcass, or mere ashes.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Self is the lord of self, who else could be the lord? With self well subdued, a man finds a lord such as few can find.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 160 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Thus must thou according to truth and nature, throughly consider how man's life is but for a very moment of time, and so depart meek and contented: even as if a ripe olive falling should praise the ground that bare her, and give thanks to the tree that begat her.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The evil done by oneself, self-begotten, self-bred, crushes the foolish, as a diamond breaks a precious stone.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 161 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Thou must be like a promontory of the sea, against which though the waves beat continually, yet it both itself stands, and about it are those swelling waves stilled and quieted.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He whose wickedness is very great brings himself down to that state where his enemy wishes him to be, as a creeper does with the tree which it surrounds.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 162 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Oh, wretched I, to whom this mischance is happened! nay, happy I, to whom this thing being happened, I can continue without grief; neither wounded by that which is present, nor in fear of that which is to come.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Bad deeds, and deeds hurtful to ourselves, are easy to do; what is beneficial and good, that is very difficult to do.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 163 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For as for this, it might have happened unto any man, but any man having such a thing befallen him, could not have continued without grief.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The foolish man who scorns the rule of the venerable (Arahat), of the elect (Ariya), of the virtuous, and follows false doctrine, he bears fruit to his own destruction, like the fruits of the Katthaka reed.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 164 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: But however, canst thou, O man! term that unhappiness, which is no mischance to the nature of man I Canst thou think that a mischance to the nature of man, which is not contrary to the end and will of his nature?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: By oneself the evil is done, by oneself one suffers; by oneself evil is left undone, by oneself one is purified. Purity and impurity belong to oneself, no one can purify another.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 165 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Doth that then which hath happened unto thee, hinder thee from being just? or magnanimous? or temperate? or wise? or circumspect? or true? or modest? or free? or from anything else of all those things in the present enjoying and possession whereof the nature of man, (as then enjoying all that is proper unto her,) is fully satisfied?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Let no one forget his own duty for the sake of another's, however great; let a man, after he has discerned his own duty, be always attentive to his duty.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 166 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Now to conclude; upon all occasion of sorrow remember henceforth to make use of this dogma, that whatsoever it is that hath happened unto thee, is in very deed no such thing of itself, as a misfortune; but that to bear it generously, is certainly great happiness.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Do not follow the evil law! Do not live on in thoughtlessness! Do not follow false doctrine! Be not a friend of the world.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 167 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: It is but an ordinary coarse one, yet it is a good effectual remedy against the fear of death, for a man to consider in his mind the examples of such, who greedily and covetously (as it were) did for a long time enjoy their lives.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Rouse thyself! do not be idle! Follow the law of virtue! The virtuous rests in bliss in this world and in the next.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 168 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Are not they themselves dead at the last? as Cadiciant's, Fabius, Julianus Lepidus, or any other who in their lifetime having buried many, were at the last buried themselves.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Follow the law of virtue; do not follow that of sin. The virtuous rests in bliss in this world and in the next.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 169 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: The whole space of any man's life, is but little; and as little as it is, with what troubles, with what manner of dispositions, and in the society of how wretched a body must it be passed!
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Look upon the world as a bubble, look upon it as a mirage: the king of death does not see him who thus looks down upon the world.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 170 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For if thou shalt look backward; behold, what an infinite chaos of time doth present itself unto thee; and as infinite a chaos, if thou shalt look forward.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Come, look at this glittering world, like unto a royal chariot; the foolish are immersed in it, but the wise do not touch it.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 171 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: In that which is so infinite, what difference can there be between that which liveth but three days, and that which liveth three ages?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He who formerly was reckless and afterwards became sober, brightens up this world, like the moon when freed from clouds.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 172 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: The most compendious, is that which is according to nature: that is, in all both words and deeds, ever to follow that which is most sound and perfect.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He whose evil deeds are covered by good deeds, brightens up this world, like the moon when freed from clouds.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 173 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For such a resolution will free a man from all trouble, strife, dissembling, and ostentation.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: This world is dark, few only can see here; a few only go to heaven, like birds escaped from the net.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 174 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: In the morning when thou findest thyself unwilling to rise, consider with thyself presently, it is to go about a man's work that I am stirred up.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The swans go on the path of the sun, they go through the ether by means of their miraculous power; the wise are led out of this world, when they have conquered Mara and his train.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 175 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Am I then yet unwilling to go about that, for which I myself was born and brought forth into this world?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If a man has transgressed one law, and speaks lies, and scoffs at another world, there is no evil he will not do.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 176 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Or was I made for this, to lay me down, and make much of myself in a warm bed? 'O but this is pleasing.' And was it then for this that thou wert born, that thou mightest enjoy pleasure?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The uncharitable do not go to the world of the gods; fools only do not praise liberality; a wise man rejoices in liberality, and through it becomes blessed in the other world.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 177 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Was it not in very truth for this, that thou mightest always be busy and in action?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Better than sovereignty over the earth, better than going to heaven, better than lordship over all worlds, is the reward of the first step in holiness.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 178 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Seest thou not how all things in the world besides, how every tree md plant, how sparrows and ants, spiders and bees: how all in their kind are intent as it were orderly to perform whatsoever (towards the preservation of this orderly universe) naturally doth become and belong unto thin?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He whose conquest is not conquered again, into whose conquest no one in this world enters, by what track can you lead him, the Awakened, the Omniscient, the trackless?
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 179 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Wilt not thou run to do that, which thy nature doth require? 'But thou must have some rest.' Yes, thou must.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He whom no desire with its snares and poisons can lead astray, by what track can you lead him, the Awakened, the Omniscient, the trackless?
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 180 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Nature hath of that also, as well as of eating and drinking, allowed thee a certain stint.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Even the gods envy those who are awakened and not forgetful, who are given to meditation, who are wise, and who delight in the repose of retirement (from the world).
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 181 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: But thou guest beyond thy stint, and beyond that which would suffice, and in matter of action, there thou comest short of that which thou mayest.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Difficult (to obtain) is the conception of men, difficult is the life of mortals, difficult is the hearing of the True Law, difficult is the birth of the Awakened (the attainment of Buddhahood).
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 182 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: It must needs be therefore, that thou dost not love thyself, for if thou didst, thou wouldst also love thy nature, and that which thy nature doth propose unto herself as her end.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Not to commit any sin, to do good, and to purify one's mind, that is the teaching of (all) the Awakened.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 183 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Others, as many as take pleasure in their trade and profession, can even pine themselves at their works, and neglect their bodies and their food for it; and doest thou less honour thy nature, than an ordinary mechanic his trade; or a good dancer his art? than a covetous man his silver, and vainglorious man applause?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The Awakened call patience the highest penance, long-suffering the highest Nirvana; for he is not an anchorite (pravragita) who strikes others, he is not an ascetic (sramana) who insults others.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 184 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: These to whatsoever they take an affection, can be content to want their meat and sleep, to further that every one which he affects: and shall actions tending to the common good of human society, seem more vile unto thee, or worthy of less respect and intention?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Not to blame, not to strike, to live restrained under the law, to be moderate in eating, to sleep and sit alone, and to dwell on the highest thoughts,--this is the teaching of the Awakened.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 185 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: How easy a thing is it for a man to put off from him all turbulent adventitious imaginations, and presently to be in perfect rest and tranquillity!
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Even in heavenly pleasures he finds no satisfaction, the disciple who is fully awakened delights only in the destruction of all desires.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 187 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Think thyself fit and worthy to speak, or to do anything that is according to nature, and let not the reproach, or report of some that may ensue upon it, ever deter thee.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Men, driven by fear, go to many a refuge, to mountains and forests, to groves and sacred trees.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 188 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: If it be right and honest to be spoken or done, undervalue not thyself so much, as to be discouraged from it.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: But that is not a safe refuge, that is not the best refuge; a man is not delivered from all pains after having gone to that refuge.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 189 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: As for them, they have their own rational over-ruling part, and their own proper inclination: which thou must not stand and look about to take notice of, but go on straight, whither both thine own particular, and the common nature do lead thee; and the way of both these, is but one.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: That is the safe refuge, that is the best refuge; having gone to that refuge, a man is delivered from all pain.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 192 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: I continue my course by actions according to nature, until I fall and cease, breathing out my last breath into that air, by which continually breathed in I did live; and falling upon that earth, out of whose gifts and fruits my father gathered his seed, my mother her blood, and my nurse her milk, out of which for so many years I have been provided, both of meat and drink.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: A supernatural person (a Buddha) is not easily found, he is not born everywhere. Wherever such a sage is born, that race prospers.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 193 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: And lastly, which beareth me that tread upon it, and beareth with me that so many ways do abuse it, or so freely make use of it, so many ways to so many ends.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Happy is the arising of the awakened, happy is the teaching of the True Law, happy is peace in the church, happy is the devotion of those who are at peace.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 194 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: No man can admire thee for thy sharp acute language, such is thy natural disability that way.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Let us live happily then, not hating those who hate us! among men who hate us let us dwell free from hatred!
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 197 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Be it so: yet there be many other good things, for the want of which thou canst not plead the want or natural ability.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Let us live happily then, free from ailments among the ailing! among men who are ailing let us dwell free from ailments!
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 198 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Let them be seen in thee, which depend wholly from thee; sincerity, gravity, laboriousness, contempt of pleasures; be not querulous, be Content with little, be kind, be free; avoid all superfluity, all vain prattling; be magnanimous.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Let us live happily then, free from greed among the greedy! among men who are greedy let us dwell free from greed!
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 199 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Doest not thou perceive, how many things there be, which notwithstanding any pretence of natural indisposition and unfitness, thou mightest have performed and exhibited, and yet still thou doest voluntarily continue drooping downwards?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Let us live happily then, though we call nothing our own! We shall be like the bright gods, feeding on happiness!
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 200 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Such there be, who when they have done a good turn to any, are ready to set them on the score for it, and to require retaliation.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Victory breeds hatred, for the conquered is unhappy. He who has given up both victory and defeat, he, the contented, is happy.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 201 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Others there be, who though they stand not upon retaliation, to require any, yet they think with themselves nevertheless, that such a one is their debtor, and they know as their word is what they have done.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: There is no fire like passion; there is no losing throw like hatred; there is no pain like this body; there is no happiness higher than rest.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 202 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Others again there be, who when they have done any such thing, do not so much as know what they have done; but are like unto the vine, which beareth her grapes, and when once she hath borne her own proper fruit, is contented and seeks for no further recompense.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Hunger is the worst of diseases, the body the greatest of pains; if one knows this truly, that is Nirvana, the highest happiness.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 203 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: As a horse after a race, and a hunting dog when he hath hunted, and a bee when she hath made her honey, look not for applause and commendation; so neither doth that man that rightly doth understand his own nature when he hath done a good turn: but from one doth proceed to do another, even as the vine after she hath once borne fruit in her own proper season, is ready for another time.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Health is the greatest of gifts, contentedness the best riches; trust is the best of relationships, Nirvana the highest happiness.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 204 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Thou therefore must be one of them, who what they do, barely do it without any further thought, and are in a manner insensible of what they do. 'Nay but,' will some reply perchance, 'this very thing a rational man is bound unto, to understand what it is, that he doeth.' For it is the property, say they, of one that is naturally sociable, to be sensible, that he doth operate sociably: nay, and to desire, that the party him self that is sociably dealt with, should be sensible of it too.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He who has tasted the sweetness of solitude and tranquillity, is free from fear and free from sin, while he tastes the sweetness of drinking in the law.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 205 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: I answer, That which thou sayest is true indeed, but the true meaning of that which is said, thou dost not understand.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The sight of the elect (Arya) is good, to live with them is always happiness; if a man does not see fools, he will be truly happy.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 206 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: But if thou dost desire to understand truly what it is that is said, fear not that thou shalt therefore give over any sociable action.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He who walks in the company of fools suffers a long way; company with fools, as with an enemy, is always painful; company with the wise is pleasure, like meeting with kinsfolk.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 207 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: The form of the Athenians' prayer did run thus: 'O rain, rain, good Jupiter, upon all the grounds and fields that belong to the Athenians.' Either we should not pray at all, or thus absolutely and freely; and not every one for himself in particular alone.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Therefore, one ought to follow the wise, the intelligent, the learned, the much enduring, the dutiful, the elect; one ought to follow a good and wise man, as the moon follows the path of the stars.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 208 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: As we say commonly, The physician hath prescribed unto this man, riding; unto another, cold baths; unto a third, to go barefoot: so it is alike to say, The nature of the universe hath prescribed unto this man sickness, or blindness, or some loss, or damage or some such thing.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He who gives himself to vanity, and does not give himself to meditation, forgetting the real aim (of life) and grasping at pleasure, will in time envy him who has exerted himself in meditation.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 209 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: And as the whole world is made up of all the particular bodies of the world, one perfect and complete body, of the same nature that particular bodies; so is the destiny of particular causes and events one general one, of the same nature that particular causes are.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Let no man ever look for what is pleasant, or what is unpleasant. Not to see what is pleasant is pain, and it is pain to see what is unpleasant.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 210 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: What I now say, even they that are mere idiots are not ignorant of: for they say commonly τοῦτο ἔφερεν ἀυτῷ, that is, This his destiny hath brought upon him.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Let, therefore, no man love anything; loss of the beloved is evil. Those who love nothing and hate nothing, have no fetters.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 211 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: This therefore is by the fates properly and particularly brought upon this, as that unto this in particular is by the physician prescribed.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: From pleasure comes grief, from pleasure comes fear; he who is free from pleasure knows neither grief nor fear.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 212 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: These therefore let us accept of in like manner, as we do those that are prescribed unto us our physicians.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: From affection comes grief, from affection comes fear; he who is free from affection knows neither grief nor fear.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 213 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For them also in themselves shall We find to contain many harsh things, but we nevertheless, in hope of health, and recovery, accept of them.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: From lust comes grief, from lust comes fear; he who is free from lust knows neither grief nor fear.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 214 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Let the fulfilling and accomplishment of those things which the common nature hath determined, be unto thee as thy health.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: From love comes grief, from love comes fear; he who is free from love knows neither grief nor fear.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 215 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Accept then, and be pleased with whatsoever doth happen, though otherwise harsh and un-pleasing, as tending to that end, to the health and welfare of the universe, and to Jove's happiness and prosperity.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: From greed comes grief, from greed comes fear; he who is free from greed knows neither grief nor fear.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 216 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For this whatsoever it be, should not have been produced, had it not conduced to the good of the universe.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He who possesses virtue and intelligence, who is just, speaks the truth, and does what is his own business, him the world will hold dear.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 217 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For neither doth any ordinary particular nature bring anything to pass, that is not to whatsoever is within the sphere of its own proper administration and government agreeable and subordinate.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He in whom a desire for the Ineffable (Nirvana) has sprung up, who is satisfied in his mind, and whose thoughts are not bewildered by love, he is called urdhvamsrotas (carried upwards by the stream).
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 218 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For these two considerations then thou must be well pleased with anything that doth happen unto thee.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Kinsmen, friends, and lovers salute a man who has been long away, and returns safe from afar.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 219 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: First, because that for thee properly it was brought to pass, and unto thee it was prescribed; and that from the very beginning by the series and connection of the first causes, it hath ever had a reference unto thee.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: In like manner his good works receive him who has done good, and has gone from this world to the other;--as kinsmen receive a friend on his return.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 220 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: And secondly, because the good success and perfect welfare, and indeed the very continuance of Him, that is the Administrator of the whole, doth in a manner depend on it.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Let a man leave anger, let him forsake pride, let him overcome all bondage! No sufferings befall the man who is not attached to name and form, and who calls nothing his own.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 221 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For the whole (because whole, therefore entire and perfect) is maimed, and mutilated, if thou shalt cut off anything at all, whereby the coherence, and contiguity as of parts, so of causes, is maintained and preserved.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He who holds back rising anger like a rolling chariot, him I call a real driver; other people are but holding the reins.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 222 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Of which certain it is, that thou doest (as much as lieth in thee) cut off, and in some sort violently take somewhat away, as often as thou art displeased with anything that happeneth.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Let a man overcome anger by love, let him overcome evil by good; let him overcome the greedy by liberality, the liar by truth!
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 223 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Be not discontented, be not disheartened, be not out of hope, if often it succeed not so well with thee punctually and precisely to do all things according to the right dogmata, but being once cast off, return unto them again: and as for those many and more frequent occurrences, either of worldly distractions, or human infirmities, which as a man thou canst not but in some measure be subject unto, be not thou discontented with them; but however, love and affect that only which thou dust return unto: a philosopher's life, and proper occupation after the most exact manner.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Speak the truth, do not yield to anger; give, if thou art asked for little; by these three steps thou wilt go near the gods.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 224 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: And when thou dust return to thy philosophy, return not unto it as the manner of some is, after play and liberty as it were, to their schoolmasters and pedagogues; but as they that have sore eyes to their sponge and egg: or as another to his cataplasm; or as others to their fomentations: so shalt not thou make it a matter of ostentation at all to obey reason but of ease and comfort.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The sages who injure nobody, and who always control their body, they will go to the unchangeable place (Nirvana), where, if they have gone, they will suffer no more.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 225 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: And remember that philosophy requireth nothing of thee, but what thy nature requireth, and wouldest thou thyself desire anything that is not according to nature? for which of these sayest thou; that which is according to nature or against it, is of itself more kind and pleasing?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Those who are ever watchful, who study day and night, and who strive after Nirvana, their passions will come to an end.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 226 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Is it not for that respect especially, that pleasure itself is to so many men's hurt and overthrow, most prevalent, because esteemed commonly most kind, and natural?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: There never was, there never will be, nor is there now, a man who is always blamed, or a man who is always praised.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 228 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: But consider well whether magnanimity rather, and true liberty, and true simplicity, and equanimity, and holiness; whether these be not most kind and natural?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Beware of bodily anger, and control thy body! Leave the sins of the body, and with thy body practise virtue!
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 231 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: And prudency itself, what more kind and amiable than it, when thou shalt truly consider with thyself, what it is through all the proper objects of thy rational intellectual faculty currently to go on without any fall or stumble?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Beware of the anger of the tongue, and control thy tongue! Leave the sins of the tongue, and practise virtue with thy tongue!
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 232 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: As for the things of the world, their true nature is in a manner so involved with obscurity, that unto many philosophers, and those no mean ones, they seemed altogether incomprehensible, and the Stoics themselves, though they judge them not altogether incomprehensible, yet scarce and not without much difficulty, comprehensible, so that all assent of ours is fallible, for who is he that is infallible in his conclusions?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Beware of the anger of the mind, and control thy mind! Leave the sins of the mind, and practise virtue with thy mind!
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 233 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: From the nature of things, pass now unto their subjects and matter: how temporary, how vile are they I such as may be in the power and possession of some abominable loose liver, of some common strumpet, of some notorious oppressor and extortioner.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The wise who control their body, who control their tongue, the wise who control their mind, are indeed well controlled.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 234 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Pass from thence to the dispositions of them that thou doest ordinarily converse with, how hardly do we bear, even with the most loving and amiable! that I may not say, how hard it is for us to bear even with our own selves, in such obscurity, and impurity of things: in such and so continual a flux both of the substances and time; both of the motions themselves, and things moved; what it is that we can fasten upon; either to honour, and respect especially; or seriously, and studiously to seek after; I cannot so much as conceive For indeed they are things contrary.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Thou art now like a sear leaf, the messengers of death (Yama) have come near to thee; thou standest at the door of thy departure, and thou hast no provision for thy journey.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 235 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Thou must comfort thyself in the expectation of thy natural dissolution, and in the meantime not grieve at the delay; but rest contented in those two things.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Make thyself an island, work hard, be wise! When thy impurities are blown away, and thou art free from guilt, thou wilt enter into the heavenly world of the elect (Ariya).
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 236 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: First, that nothing shall happen unto thee, which is not according to the nature of the universe.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Thy life has come to an end, thou art come near to death (Yama), there is no resting-place for thee on the road, and thou hast no provision for thy journey.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 237 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Secondly, that it is in thy power, to do nothing against thine own proper God, and inward spirit.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Make thyself an island, work hard, be wise! When thy impurities are blown away, and thou art free from guilt, thou wilt not enter again into birth and decay.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 238 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For it is not in any man's power to constrain thee to transgress against him.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Let a wise man blow off the impurities of his self, as a smith blows off the impurities of silver one by one, little by little, and from time to time.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 239 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Thus from time to time and upon all occasions thou must put this question to thyself; what is now that part of mine which they call the rational mistress part, employed about?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: As the impurity which springs from the iron, when it springs from it, destroys it; thus do a transgressor's own works lead him to the evil path.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 240 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Whose soul do I now properly possess? a child's? or a youth's? a woman's? or a tyrant's? some brute, or some wild beast's soul?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The taint of prayers is non-repetition; the taint of houses, non-repair; the taint of the body is sloth; the taint of a watchman, thoughtlessness.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 241 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: What those things are in themselves, which by the greatest part are esteemed good, thou mayest gather even from this.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Bad conduct is the taint of woman, greediness the taint of a benefactor; tainted are all evil ways in this world and in the next.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 242 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For if a man shall hear things mentioned as good, which are really good indeed, such as are prudence, temperance, justice, fortitude, after so much heard and conceived, he cannot endure to hear of any more, for the word good is properly spoken of them.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: But there is a taint worse than all taints,--ignorance is the greatest taint. O mendicants! throw off that taint, and become taintless!
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 243 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: But as for those which by the vulgar are esteemed good, if he shall hear them mentioned as good, he doth hearken for more.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Life is easy to live for a man who is without shame, a crow hero, a mischief-maker, an insulting, bold, and wretched fellow.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 244 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: He is well contented to hear, that what is spoken by the comedian, is but familiarly and popularly spoken, so that even the vulgar apprehend the difference.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: But life is hard to live for a modest man, who always looks for what is pure, who is disinterested, quiet, spotless, and intelligent.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 245 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For why is it else, that this offends not and needs not to be excused, when virtues are styled good: but that which is spoken in commendation of wealth, pleasure, or honour, we entertain it only as merrily and pleasantly spoken?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: And the man who gives himself to drinking intoxicating liquors, he, even in this world, digs up his own root.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 247 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Proceed therefore, and inquire further, whether it may not be that those things also which being mentioned upon the stage were merrily, and with great applause of the multitude, scoffed at with this jest, that they that possessed them had not in all the world of their own, (such was their affluence and plenty) so much as a place where to avoid their excrements.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: O man, know this, that the unrestrained are in a bad state; take care that greediness and vice do not bring thee to grief for a long time!
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 248 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Whether, I say, those ought not also in very deed to be much respected, and esteemed of, as the only things that are truly good.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The world gives according to their faith or according to their pleasure: if a man frets about the food and the drink given to others, he will find no rest either by day or by night.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 249 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: No corruption can reduce either of these unto nothing: for neither did I of nothing become a subsistent creature.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He in whom that feeling is destroyed, and taken out with the very root, finds rest by day and by night.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 250 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Every part of mine then will by mutation be disposed into a certain part of the whole world, and that in time into another part; and so in infinitum; by which kind of mutation, I also became what I am, and so did they that begot me, and they before them, and so upwards in infinitum.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: There is no fire like passion, there is no shark like hatred, there is no snare like folly, there is no torrent like greed.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 251 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For so we may be allowed to speak, though the age and government of the world, be to some certain periods of time limited, and confined.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The fault of others is easily perceived, but that of oneself is difficult to perceive; a man winnows his neighbour's faults like chaff, but his own fault he hides, as a cheat hides the bad die from the gambler.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 252 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Reason, and rational power, are faculties which content themselves with themselves, and their own proper operations.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If a man looks after the faults of others, and is always inclined to be offended, his own passions will grow, and he is far from the destruction of passions.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 253 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: And as for their first inclination and motion, that they take from themselves.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: There is no path through the air, a man is not a Samana by outward acts. The world delights in vanity, the Tathagatas (the Buddhas) are free from vanity.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 254 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: But their progress is right to the end and object, which is in their way, as it were, and lieth just before them: that is, which is feasible and possible, whether it be that which at the first they proposed to themselves, or no.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: There is no path through the air, a man is not a Samana by outward acts. No creatures are eternal; but the awakened (Buddha) are never shaken.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 255 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For which reason also such actions are termed κατορθώσεις, to intimate the directness of the way, by which they are achieved.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: A man is not learned because he talks much; he who is patient, free from hatred and fear, he is called learned.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 258 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Nothing must be thought to belong to a man, which doth not belong unto him as he is a man.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: A man is not a supporter of the law because he talks much; even if a man has learnt little, but sees the law bodily, he is a supporter of the law, a man who never neglects the law.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 259 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: The final ends and consummations of actions are nothing at all to a man's nature.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He in whom there is truth, virtue, love, restraint, moderation, he who is free from impurity and is wise, he is called an elder.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 261 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: The end therefore of a man, or the summum bonum whereby that end is fulfilled, cannot consist in the consummation of actions purposed and intended.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: An envious greedy, dishonest man does not become respectable by means of much talking only, or by the beauty of his complexion.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 262 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Again, concerning these outward worldly things, were it so that any of them did properly belong unto man, then would it not belong unto man, to condemn them and to stand in opposition with them.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He in whom all this is destroyed, and taken out with the very root, he, when freed from hatred and wise, is called respectable.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 263 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Neither would he be praiseworthy that can live without them; or he good, (if these were good indeed) who of his own accord doth deprive himself of any of them.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Not by tonsure does an undisciplined man who speaks falsehood become a Samana; can a man be a Samana who is still held captive by desire and greediness?
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 264 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: But we see contrariwise, that the more a man doth withdraw himself from these wherein external pomp and greatness doth consist, or any other like these; or the better he doth bear with the loss of these, the better he is accounted.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He who always quiets the evil, whether small or large, he is called a Samana (a quiet man), because he has quieted all evil.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 265 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Such as thy thoughts and ordinary cogitations are, such will thy mind be in time.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: A man is not a mendicant (Bhikshu) simply because he asks others for alms; he who adopts the whole law is a Bhikshu, not he who only begs.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 266 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For the soul doth as it were receive its tincture from the fancies, and imaginations.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He who is above good and evil, who is chaste, who with knowledge passes through the world, he indeed is called a Bhikshu.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 267 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Dye it therefore and thoroughly soak it with the assiduity of these cogitations.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: A man is not an elect (Ariya) because he injures living creatures; because he has pity on all living creatures, therefore is a man called Ariya.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 270 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Wheresoever thou mayest live, there it is in thy power to live well and happy.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The best of ways is the eightfold; the best of truths the four words; the best of virtues passionlessness; the best of men he who has eyes to see.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 273 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: But thou mayest live at the Court, there then also mayest thou live well and happy.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: This is the way, there is no other that leads to the purifying of intelligence. Go on this way! Everything else is the deceit of Mara (the tempter).
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 274 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Again, that which everything is made for, he is also made unto that, and cannot but naturally incline unto it.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If you go on this way, you will make an end of pain! The way was preached by me, when I had understood the removal of the thorns (in the flesh).
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 275 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Wherein the end of everything doth consist, therein also doth his good and benefit consist.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: You yourself must make an effort. The Tathagatas (Buddhas) are only preachers. The thoughtful who enter the way are freed from the bondage of Mara.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 276 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For that we are made for society, it hath long since been demonstrated.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: `All created things perish,' he who knows and sees this becomes passive in pain; this is the way to purity.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 277 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Or can any man make any question of this, that whatsoever is naturally worse and inferior, is ordinarily subordinated to that which is better? and that those things that are best, are made one for another?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: `All created things are grief and pain,' he who knows and sees this becomes passive in pain; this is the way that leads to purity.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 278 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: And those things that have souls, are better than those that have none? and of those that have, those best that have rational souls?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: `All forms are unreal,' he who knows and sees this becomes passive in pain; this is the way that leads to purity.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 279 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: But it is a thing impossible, that wicked man should not commit some such things.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He who does not rouse himself when it is time to rise, who, though young and strong, is full of sloth, whose will and thought are weak, that lazy and idle man will never find the way to knowledge.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 280 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Neither doth anything happen to any man, which in the ordinary course of nature as natural unto him doth not happen.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Watching his speech, well restrained in mind, let a man never commit any wrong with his body! Let a man but keep these three roads of action clear, and he will achieve the way which is taught by the wise.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 281 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: And truly, if either he that is ignorant that such a thing hath happened unto him, or he that is ambitious to be commended for his magnanimity, can be patient, and is not grieved: is it not a grievous thing, that either ignorance, or a vain desire to please and to be commended, should be more powerful and effectual than true prudence?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Through zeal knowledge is gotten, through lack of zeal knowledge is lost; let a man who knows this double path of gain and loss thus place himself that knowledge may grow.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 282 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: As for the things themselves, they touch not the soul, neither can they have any access unto it: neither can they of themselves any ways either affect it, or move it.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Cut down the whole forest (of lust), not a tree only! Danger comes out of the forest (of lust). When you have cut down both the forest (of lust) and its undergrowth, then, Bhikshus, you will be rid of the forest and free!
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 283 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For she herself alone can affect and move herself, and according as the dogmata and opinions are, which she doth vouchsafe herself; so are those things which, as accessories, have any co-existence with her.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: So long as the love of man towards women, even the smallest, is not destroyed, so long is his mind in bondage, as the calf that drinks milk is to its mother.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 284 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: After one consideration, man is nearest unto us; as we are bound to do them good, and to bear with them.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Cut out the love of self, like an autumn lotus, with thy hand! Cherish the road of peace. Nirvana has been shown by Sugata (Buddha).
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 285 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: But as he may oppose any of our true proper actions, so man is unto me but as a thing indifferent: even as the sun, or the wind, or some wild beast.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: `Here I shall dwell in the rain, here in winter and summer,' thus the fool meditates, and does not think of his death.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 286 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: By some of these it may be, that some operation or other of mine, may be hindered; however, of my mind and resolution itself, there can be no let or impediment, by reason of that ordinary constant both exception (or reservation wherewith it inclineth) and ready conversion of objects; from that which may not be, to that which may be, which in the prosecution of its inclinations, as occasion serves, it doth observe.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Death comes and carries off that man, praised for his children and flocks, his mind distracted, as a flood carries off a sleeping village.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 287 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For by these the mind doth turn and convert any impediment whatsoever, to be her aim and purpose.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Sons are no help, nor a father, nor relations; there is no help from kinsfolk for one whom death has seized.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 288 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: So that what before was the impediment, is now the principal object of her working; and that which before was in her way, is now her readiest way.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: A wise and good man who knows the meaning of this, should quickly clear the way that leads to Nirvana.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 289 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Honour that which is chiefest and most powerful in the world, and that is it, which makes use of all things, and governs all things.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If by leaving a small pleasure one sees a great pleasure, let a wise man leave the small pleasure, and look to the great.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 290 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: So also in thyself; honour that which is chiefest, and most powerful; and is of one kind and nature with that which we now spake of.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He who, by causing pain to others, wishes to obtain pleasure for himself, he, entangled in the bonds of hatred, will never be free from hatred.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 291 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For it is the very same, which being in thee, turneth all other things to its own use, and by whom also thy life is governed.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: What ought to be done is neglected, what ought not to be done is done; the desires of unruly, thoughtless people are always increasing.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 292 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: This rule thou must remember to apply and make use of upon every conceit and apprehension of wrong.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: But they whose whole watchfulness is always directed to their body, who do not follow what ought not to be done, and who steadfastly do what ought to be done, the desires of such watchful and wise people will come to an end.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 293 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: And if the whole be not, why should I make it my private grievance? consider rather what it is wherein he is overseen that is thought to have done the wrong.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: A true Brahmana goes scatheless, though he have killed father and mother, and two valiant kings, though he has destroyed a kingdom with all its subjects.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 294 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Again, often meditate how swiftly all things that subsist, and all things that are done in the world, are carried away, and as it were conveyed out of sight: for both the substance themselves, we see as a flood, are in a continual flux; and all actions in a perpetual change; and the causes themselves, subject to a thousand alterations, neither is there anything almost, that may ever be said to be now settled and constant.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: A true Brahmana goes scatheless, though he have killed father and mother, and two holy kings, and an eminent man besides.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 295 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Next unto this, and which follows upon it, consider both the infiniteness of the time already past, and the immense vastness of that which is to come, wherein all things are to be resolved and annihilated.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The disciples of Gotama (Buddha) are always well awake, and their thoughts day and night are always set on Buddha.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 296 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Art not thou then a very fool, who for these things, art either puffed up with pride, or distracted with cares, or canst find in thy heart to make such moans as for a thing that would trouble thee for a very long time?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The disciples of Gotama are always well awake, and their thoughts day and night are always set on the law.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 297 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Consider the whole universe whereof thou art but a very little part, and the whole age of the world together, whereof but a short and very momentary portion is allotted unto thee, and all the fates and destinies together, of which how much is it that comes to thy part and share!
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The disciples of Gotama are always well awake, and their thoughts day and night are always set on the church.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 298 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: I for my part am in the meantime in possession of as much, as the common nature would have me to possess: and that which mine own nature would have me do, I do.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The disciples of Gotama are always well awake, and their thoughts day and night are always set on their body.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 299 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Let not that chief commanding part of thy soul be ever subject to any variation through any corporal either pain or pleasure, neither suffer it to be mixed with these, but let it both circumscribe itself, and confine those affections to their own proper parts and members.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The disciples of Gotama are always well awake, and their mind day and night always delights in compassion.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 300 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: But if at any time they do reflect and rebound upon the mind and understanding (as in an united and compacted body it must needs;) then must thou not go about to resist sense and feeling, it being natural.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: The disciples of Gotama are always well awake, and their mind day and night always delights in meditation.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 301 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: However let not thy understanding to this natural sense and feeling, which whether unto our flesh pleasant or painful, is unto us nothing properly, add an opinion of either good or bad and all is well.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: It is hard to leave the world (to become a friar), it is hard to enjoy the world; hard is the monastery, painful are the houses; painful it is to dwell with equals (to share everything in common) and the itinerant mendicant is beset with pain. Therefore let no man be an itinerant mendicant and he will not be beset with pain.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 302 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: He liveth with the Gods, who at all times affords unto them the spectacle of a soul, both contented and well pleased with whatsoever is afforded, or allotted unto her; and performing whatsoever is pleasing to that Spirit, whom (being part of himself) Jove hath appointed to every man as his overseer and governor.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Whatever place a faithful, virtuous, celebrated, and wealthy man chooses, there he is respected.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 303 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Be not angry neither with him whose breath, neither with him whose arm holes, are offensive.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Good people shine from afar, like the snowy mountains; bad people are not seen, like arrows shot by night.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 304 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: What can he do? such is his breath naturally, and such are his arm holes; and from such, such an effect, and such a smell must of necessity proceed. 'O, but the man (sayest thou) hath understanding in him, and might of himself know, that he by standing near, cannot choose but offend.' And thou also (God bless thee!) hast understanding.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He alone who, without ceasing, practises the duty of sitting alone and sleeping alone, he, subduing himself, will rejoice in the destruction of all desires alone, as if living in a forest.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 305 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Let thy reasonable faculty, work upon his reasonable faculty; show him his fault, admonish him.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: He who says what is not, goes to hell; he also who, having done a thing, says I have not done it. After death both are equal, they are men with evil deeds in the next world.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 306 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: If he hearken unto thee, thou hast cured him, and there will be no more occasion of anger.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Many men whose shoulders are covered with the yellow gown are ill-conditioned and unrestrained; such evil-doers by their evil deeds go to hell.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 307 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: As thou dost purpose to live, when thou hast retired thyself to some such place, where neither roarer nor harlot is: so mayest thou here.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Better it would be to swallow a heated iron ball, like flaring fire, than that a bad unrestrained fellow should live on the charity of the land.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 308 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: And if they will not suffer thee, then mayest thou leave thy life rather than thy calling, but so as one that doth not think himself anyways wronged.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Four things does a wreckless man gain who covets his neighbour's wife,--a bad reputation, an uncomfortable bed, thirdly, punishment, and lastly, hell.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 309 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Now till some such thing force me out, I will continue free; neither shall any man hinder me to do what I will, and my will shall ever be by the proper nature of a reasonable and sociable creature, regulated and directed.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: There is bad reputation, and the evil way (to hell), there is the short pleasure of the frightened in the arms of the frightened, and the king imposes heavy punishment; therefore let no man think of his neighbour's wife.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 310 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: That rational essence by which the universe is governed, is for community and society; and therefore hath it both made the things that are worse, for the best, and hath allied and knit together those which are best, as it were in an harmony.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: As a grass-blade, if badly grasped, cuts the arm, badly-practised asceticism leads to hell.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 311 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Seest thou not how it hath sub-ordinated, and co-ordinated? and how it hath distributed unto everything according to its worth? and those which have the pre-eminency and superiority above all, hath it united together, into a mutual consent and agreement.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: An act carelessly performed, a broken vow, and hesitating obedience to discipline, all this brings no great reward.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 312 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: How hast thou carried thyself hitherto towards the Gods? towards thy parents? towards thy brethren? towards thy wife? towards thy children? towards thy masters? thy foster-fathers? thy friends? thy domestics? thy servants?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: If anything is to be done, let a man do it, let him attack it vigorously! A careless pilgrim only scatters the dust of his passions more widely.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 313 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Is it so with thee, that hitherto thou hast neither by word or deed wronged any of them?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: An evil deed is better left undone, for a man repents of it afterwards; a good deed is better done, for having done it, one does not repent.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 314 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Remember withal through how many things thou hast already passed, and how many thou hast been able to endure; so that now the legend of thy life is full, and thy charge is accomplished.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Like a well-guarded frontier fort, with defences within and without, so let a man guard himself. Not a moment should escape, for they who allow the right moment to pass, suffer pain when they are in hell.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 315 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Doth either the sun take upon him to do that which belongs to the rain? or his son Aesculapius that, which unto the earth doth properly belong?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: They who are ashamed of what they ought not to be ashamed of, and are not ashamed of what they ought to be ashamed of, such men, embracing false doctrines enter the evil path.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 316 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Though they all differ one from another, and have their several charges and functions by themselves, do they not all nevertheless concur and co- operate to one end?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: They who fear when they ought not to fear, and fear not when they ought to fear, such men, embracing false doctrines, enter the evil path.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 317 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: If so be that the Gods have deliberated in particular of those things that should happen unto me, I must stand to their deliberation, as discrete and wise.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: They who forbid when there is nothing to be forbidden, and forbid not when there is something to be forbidden, such men, embracing false doctrines, enter the evil path.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 318 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: For that a God should be an imprudent God, is a thing hard even to conceive: and why should they resolve to do me hurt? for what profit either unto them or the universe (which they specially take care for) could arise from it?
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: They who know what is forbidden as forbidden, and what is not forbidden as not forbidden, such men, embracing the true doctrine, enter the good path.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 319 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: But if so be that they have not deliberated of me in particular, certainly they have of the whole in general, and those things which in consequence and coherence of this general deliberation happen unto me in particular, I am bound to embrace and accept of.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Silently shall I endure abuse as the elephant in battle endures the arrow sent from the bow: for the world is ill-natured.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 320 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Now that unto every one is most profitable, which is according to his own constitution and nature.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: They lead a tamed elephant to battle, the king mounts a tamed elephant; the tamed is the best among men, he who silently endures abuse.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 321 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: And my nature is, to be rational in all my actions and as a good, and natural member of a city and commonwealth, towards my fellow members ever to be sociably and kindly disposed and affected.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: Mules are good, if tamed, and noble Sindhu horses, and elephants with large tusks; but he who tames himself is better still.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 322 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: My city and country as I am Antoninus, is Rome; as a man, the whole world.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn

text: For with these animals does no man reach the untrodden country (Nirvana), where a tamed man goes on a tamed animal, viz. on his own well-tamed self.
author: Phật Thích Ca · Kinh Pháp Cú
source: Pháp Cú · kệ 323 · bản Anh F. Max Müller

text: Those things therefore that are expedient and profitable to those cities, are the only things that are good and expedient for me.
author: Marcus Aurelius
source: Meditations · bản Anh Meric Casaubon · trích đoạn
